messages_body:
Hi Sofia / Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on the use case and success criteria. Attached is a concise POC proposal (acme-poc-proposal.pdf) and a first-pass evaluation plan. High-level recap and asks: 

- Goal: validate Redwood inference for ACME search augmentation (latency and relevance)
- Proposed POC length: 4 weeks (pilot + 3 week eval)
- Success criteria (proposed): 95th percentile latency < 200ms; semantic relevance (NDCG@10) lift > 12% vs baseline; false positive rate < 5% for critical intents; operational cost target: <$0.60 per 1k tokens
- Evaluation options: offline held-out eval, online shadowing, or hybrid (recommend hybrid)

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm success criteria and ownership of labels/metrics
2) We share the evaluation rubric and a sample dataset (Redwood will keep infra and run metrics)
3) Procurement loop for SOW and security paperwork
4) Target kickoff week of Apr 18 (flexible)

Ive cc'd Rachel to help with evaluation & instrumentation questions. Please let me know any immediate blockers.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
Marissa,

Thanks — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- On success criteria, ACME will hold to: latency 95th < 200ms; relevance uplift target 10-15% (we'll confirm the exact metric after a sample run); error rate thresholds OK
- We prefer a hybrid approach: primarily offline tests to validate model quality, then a short shadow window on real traffic to confirm behaviour before production rollout
- Procurement: looping in Linh (procurement) to start SOW review and any compliance docs

We can aim for kickoff the week of Apr 18 — Tom and I are available then.

Sofia Alvarez
Director of Search & Personalization | ACME Corp
sofia@acme.com
Thanks Sofia — appreciate the clarity.

Two quick notes on methodology:
1) Offline evals: Redwood will run the held-out datasets against candidate model variants and produce the NDCG/precision/recall tables. Pros: fast iterations, controlled comparisons. Cons: may miss production edge cases.
2) Online shadow: mirror a small fraction of live queries to Redwood (no user impact) and collect ACME labels on a sample. Pros: catches real-world distribution; Cons: requires instrumentation and a short labeling sprint.

Proposed ownership model: ACME owns business-signal labeling and final pass/fail decisions; Redwood will run the infra, produce metrics, and provide tooling for labeling exports. For the rubric, I propose pass thresholds and severity tiers (blocker/major/minor) — I'll attach an updated doc and a suggested rubric table.

Cc'ing Dylan to loop him in on instrumentation questions.

If that sounds good I'll update the eval plan and share a Drive link + HubSpot deal card with milestones.

Best,
Marissa

Tom / Sofia / team,

Thanks — I've updated the evaluation plan and attached acme-poc-eval-plan.docx (drive link also above). Key updates included:
- Detailed grading rubric (pass thresholds by metric and severity tiers)
- Exact deliverables per week: week 0 kick-off & access; week 1 offline runs; week 2 shadow window + labeling; week 3 analysis + recommendations
- Owners: ACME — label quality & business sign-off; Redwood — model hosting, infra, and metric dumps; Redwood/ACME joint — analysis and remediation plan

Grading rubric (summary):
- Blocker: model produces critical failures on core intents (fail POC)
- Major: metrics below threshold that materially affect UX (requires remediation + conditional pass)
- Minor: edge cases / acceptable degradation requiring follow-up

Next steps I will take: upload final doc to Drive, create HubSpot milestones, and draft SOW for Linh. Please confirm kickoff date (Apr 18) and dataset delivery estimate.
